title: Technical Contributions to AI Governance | NIST

policy_extraction.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
covered_actors: NIST Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) AI Program
Federal offices and interagency AI bodies (NAIAC, NSTC Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Subcommittee, NITRD AI Working Group, ICSP AISCWG, National AI Research Resource Task Force)
U.S. Department of Commerce International Trade Administration and U.S. Department of State
International governance forums and bilateral partners (OECD, G7 Hiroshima Process, Asia, Middle East, North America)

evidence.quote: The Program plays a key role as a neutral convener of organizations and individuals with disparate views about AI matters.

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Brief NIST ITL AI Program informational overview (originally published 2021-07-26 and later updated to reference the 2023 G7 Hiroshima Process) summarizing NIST's role as a neutral technical convener, federal AI standards coordinator, and interagency/international AI governance participant. Contains no operative compliance requirements or enforcement hooks.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: This short institutional overview has sparse explicit rationale language, centered primarily on innovation_enablement: grounding domestic and international AI governance in scientific and technical realities through neutral convening, federal standards coordination, and shared research infrastructure (NAIRR) to shape effective AI development. Consumer_public_safety appears modestly via the goal of 'effective and reliable AI,' and economic_competitiveness plays a minor role through partnerships with the International Trade Administration in international governance.

evidence_spans.quote: The agency’s active participation in national and international discussions helps to shape the development of effective and reliable AI and ground AI governance in technical realities.

provides scientific and technical expertise and contributions to national and international discussions on AI governance. The Program plays a key role as a neutral convener of organizations and individuals with disparate views about AI matters.
On many of these efforts, the Program partners with other agencies, including the U.S. Department of Commerce’s International Trade Administration and the U.S. Department of State.
